reader_situation: Someone wondering whether to switch their dishwasher from heated dry to air dry wants to know how much money each load actually costs and whether it's worth wet plastic containers.
direct_answer: On an ENERGY STAR certified standard dishwasher, heated dry costs less than about 10 cents a load at the US average of 17-18 cents per kWh, and likely well under that. No manufacturer or agency publishes a typical per-cycle drying figure, but the whole certified cycle is capped at about 1.12 kWh (240 kWh/year over 215 cycles), and most of a dishwasher's energy goes to heating water. A plug-in watt meter gives your own model's exact number.
consensus: Air dry saves energy compared with heated dry.
Crack the door after the cycle to help air drying.
Use rinse aid for better drying.
Run full loads and skip pre-rinsing.
Dishwashers use less water and energy than hand washing.
gaps: Most articles quote a per-load heated-dry figure without a source; none of the agency pages reviewed publish one. The defensible number is a ceiling built from ENERGY STAR's cap and LBNL's energy split.
ENERGY STAR's standard-size limit is 240 kWh/year at 215 cycles/year, including drying energy: 240 / 215 = about 1.12 kWh per complete cycle, or 19-20 cents at 17-18 cents/kWh.

Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory's Home Energy Saver documentation says the majority of a dishwasher's energy goes to water heating; machine energy covers pumps and the heating elements for drying. So pumps plus drying are under half of 1.12 kWh, under about 0.56 kWh, under about 10 cents a load.
LBNL's model assumes 0.78 kWh/load of machine energy for older machines (based on 1990 DOE data), so older dishwashers can use more for the machine side.
A plug-in watt meter measures real use (registry); running one load with heated dry and one without isolates the drying cost, because drying draws no hot water from the water heater.

NRCan says most users pick the same high-temperature program every time and recommends eco mode plus the air-dry setting; ENERGY STAR lists the ability to turn off heated dry as a feature to look for.
Hand washing: ENERGY STAR says a certified dishwasher uses less than half the energy of hand washing and saves about 8,400 gallons of water a year.

evidence.claim: ENERGY STAR energy cap and annual cycles
evidence.detail: Standard (8+ place settings): max 240 kWh/year and 3.2 gallons/cycle; compact: 155 kWh/year and 2.0 gallons/cycle. Average cycles per year is 215. Drying energy is part of the overall energy calculation. Test method: DOE 10 CFR 430 Subpart B Appendix C1.
evidence.source_title: Dishwashers Key Product Criteria | ENERGY STAR

evidence.detail: A standard ENERGY STAR certified dishwasher costs about $50 per year to run; compared with hand washing it saves 8,400 gallons of water each year, uses less than half as much energy, saves about $220 per year and over 230 hours of personal time. Scrape instead of rinsing; run full loads; look for the ability to turn off heated dry.

evidence.claim: Most dishwasher energy is water heating
evidence.detail: Total dishwasher energy = machine energy + water heating energy; the majority of the energy is used for water heating. Both depend directly on the number of loads washed.
evidence.source_title: Home Energy Saver & Score Engineering Documentation: Dishwasher Energy Consumption (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)

evidence.claim: Machine energy includes the drying heaters
evidence.detail: Machine energy, the energy to run a load including pumps and heating elements for the drying cycle, is assumed to be 0.78 kWh/load (citing US DOE 1990, Table 3.4).
evidence.source_title: Home Energy Saver & Score Engineering Documentation: Machine Energy (Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)

evidence.claim: Use air dry and eco mode
evidence.detail: An ENERGY STAR certified dishwasher uses on average 12% less energy and 30% less water than a standard model. No need to pre-rinse. The majority of users choose the same setting all the time, usually a high-temperature program; use eco mode. Turn on the air-dry setting instead of heat-dry.
evidence.source_title: Use your dishwasher more efficiently for big savings (Natural Resources Canada)

evidence.claim: Canadian minimum standards include power-dry reporting
evidence.detail: Standard dishwashers: maximum total annual energy consumption 307 kWh and water 18.93 L/cycle; compact 222 kWh and 13.25 L/cycle; test standard CAN/CSA-C373-14; reports list drying options including power-dry with fan and heat on.
evidence.source_title: Dishwashers - Energy efficiency regulations (Natural Resources Canada)

real_questions: How much does heated dry cost per load?
Why are my plastics still wet with air dry?
Is hand washing cheaper than the dishwasher?

original_asset.spec: Ceiling math: 240 kWh / 215 cycles = 1.12 kWh per cycle; x 17-18 cents = 19-20 cents; half of 1.12 = 0.56 kWh x 17-18 cents = 9.5-10 cents per load; x 215 cycles = about $20-22/year ceiling for pumps plus drying. Plus a two-load watt-meter test with the formula (kWh with heat - kWh without) x rate x loads per year.

cautions: Don't present an unsourced per-load drying kWh as typical.
Watt meter only works if the dishwasher plugs into an outlet; don't open hardwired junction boxes.
Use the registry electricity rate and formula.
